mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 30 months (t-test p > 0.05) during high-inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) combined with UNRATE below 7% predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as strong labor demand supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE < 7% in the current month
failure_condition: Rank IC of the interaction < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon in expanding labor markets.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (industrial production) exceeding 2% for two months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals accelerating economic activity and investor optimism.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the production surge (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 98.5 triggers a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates supply-side weakness and potential earnings compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 98.5 in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05) during supply shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) over three months followed by a rise in FEDFUNDS below 3% predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 return as the market anticipates disinflation and rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for 3 months then FEDFUNDS < 3% in the fourth month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the regime conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 6% and PAYEMS exceeds 130,000 in a month, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 60-day return as low unemployment and strong hiring boost equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 6% and PAYEMS > 130000 in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive return over 60 days (p-value > 0.05) in such labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in RSAFS (retail sales) below 400 million dollars in a month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak retail demand signals economic weakness.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically negative (p-value > 0.05) during recession precursors.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in GDPC1 (GDP) by over 2% in the last quarter followed by a hold in FEDFUNDS at < 4% for two months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate continued economic contraction and no policy easing.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 down >2% QoQ and FEDFUNDS < 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.05) in slowdown phases.
